Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.

args.text: The proposal changes retail distribution across the district. Trade competition from the new supermarket is not considered. There is demand for the development in this area. There is demand for the project. The viability of the centre may be affected. Views from private properties are not an effect. Loss of views from private land. Pedestrian safety is assessed under clause 7(1)(f) of Schedule 4. Under cl. 7 (1) (f) the safety of the road is assessed. Matters under cl 7(1)(f) are covered. Safety is covered by cl 7(1)(a). Special circumstances apply under section 95A(9). We rely on s95A (9) for notification. There are special circumstances here. Section 95B(10) is relied on. The National Policy Direction requires this. The Natural Environment Act sets the standard. The NEA applies to the site. The Planning Act 2026 national standards apply to the site. The Planning Act 2026, through its instruments, directs this. The national standards apply under the Planning Act. The Planning Act 2026 sets the process. We have not relied on the National Policy Direction. s104(1C) prevents reliance on the NEA. Section 104(1C) bars the use of the Natural Environment Act. This prevents reliance on the NEA. No regard is given to the NEA. Nor do we apply the National Policy Direction. The National Policy Direction is cited, without relying on it. The NEA is excluded from reliance. An ITA is required under E27.6.1. E27.6.1 requires an integrated transport assessment. The integrated transport assessment is mandatory under E27.6.1. An ITA is required. E27.6.1 may require an ITA. The activity requires an ITA because E27.6.1 is exceeded. Auckland Transport is the road controlling authority. Auckland Transport, as RCA, must approve it. AT is the RCA for this road. The works (AT) are the road controlling authority. The road controlling authority is Auckland Transport. The road controlling authority, AT, agreed. The road controlling authority was AT. Auckland Council is the road controlling authority. The BCR is MBCM compliant. The result is compliant with the MBCM. The BCR follows MBCM-compliant methods. The BCR follows the MBCM. The TMDG statistics show the model is fit for purpose. Transport Model Development Guidelines show fitness for purpose. The TMDG statistics are reported. The model is fit-for-purpose. RASF is mandatory for developers. The Roads and Streets Framework must comply. The RASF is a useful guide. The Roads and Streets Framework requires developers to follow it. RASF is binding on the applicant. Traffic effects are less than minor. The road is safe.
